title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At 12 of the 13 epoch starts up to 1.7·109 steps this machine's configuration is identical, cell for cell, to that of 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF (it gets there about 1.5 times later); so it runs the same running-parity computation. Lean proves eleven shift rules over its 4-cell words. It halts only when B stands left of a cell holding 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: A with 0 under the head, 1 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Shift rules over the 4-cell words
claims.text: D runs left over 1111 leaving it (on a 0) or writing 0101 (on a 1); E runs left over 1111 writing 1010; E, F, A cross 0101, 1010 going right, D and E going left.

claims.title: Same epoch starts as its twin
claims.text: The epoch starts (a crossing of 80% of the tape) of this machine at steps 3,350, 8,689, 19,594, 72,335, 220,328, 734,951, 2,145,468, 6,420,857, 60,731,203, 186,137,520, 574,984,133 and 1,744,002,084 have exactly the configuration (tape, head position, state) of 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF at its steps 2,284, 5,873, 13,248, 47,799, 145,962, 487,979, 1,427,948, 4,277,179, 40,483,837, 124,076,294, 383,276,545 and 1,162,585,978. (The epoch near 2·10<sup>7</sup> was sampled at different turns in the two runs.) Left end at 56, 103, 172, 374, ... 68,091 cells, as for the twin.

claims.title: What it computes
claims.text: As for the twin: a binary word in letters u = 1110, v = 1111, replaced on each leftward sweep by its running XOR, giving Sierpinski triangles in space-time, in epochs growing by about 1.75. Inferred from the identical epoch starts.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: Only C reading 1 halts; C is entered only from B (1RC on 0, 0RC on 1), so the machine halts exactly when B stands just left of a 1 (B> x 1). Read off the table.

claims.title: No closed tape language with small windows
claims.text: bbtools.ctl K = 3..6 leaves halting configurations; n-gram CPS 3 to 7 fails; no invariant mod 2..12.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 47,528 cells have been visited and 37,059 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.04).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The two twins agree at epoch starts; between them they take different routes (this one about 1.5 times slower), and each has its own halting pattern, so a proof for one would have to be redone for the other unless the agreement itself is proved.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: 1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF goes through 4,995,966 configurations of 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF in its first 10<sup>7</sup> steps, in order, about 1.5 times slower. The same table as 1RB---_0RC1RD_1LA0LA_1LE0RB_1LF1LE_1LC0LD up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RB_1LC---_0LA1LD_1RE0LC_1RF1RE_1RA0RD up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_1RE0RE_1LF---_0LD1LA up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RA_1RC0RF_1RD0RD_1LE---_0LC1LF_1RA0LE up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 47,528 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: The same computation as another holdout
html:
Run this machine and 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF side by side and look at the moments when the head starts a sweep across the whole tape. This machine gets there later (step 72,335 instead of 47,799, 1,744,002,084 instead of 1,162,585,978), but the tape is the same cell for cell, with the head on the same cell in the same state (E reading 1). That holds at 12 of the 13 epoch starts up to 1.7·109 steps.

At step 72,335 both tapes begin

1^12 0 1^7 0 1^7 0 1^3 0 1^15 0 1^3 0 1^3 0 1^15 0 1^7 0 ...

sections.heading: Running parity, Sierpinski triangles
html: The tape is a word in two 4-cell letters, 1110 and 1111 (blocks 14k+30). In the twin, each leftward sweep provably replaces the word by its running XOR; here the same words are crossed with different states (D, E, F, A: eleven shift rules proved in Lean), more slowly. The space-time diagram shows the same Sierpinski triangles and the same epochs, each about 1.75 times longer than the last.

sections.heading: Only when B stands left of a 1
html: The only halting transition is C reading 1, and C is entered only from B, which always moves right. So the machine stops exactly when B stands just left of a cell holding 1. As for its twin, the question is in the rightward sweeps and the turns at the walls, which were not decoded.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.04).
After 109 steps the tape spans 47,528 cells (38,068 left of the start, 115 right), with a density of 1s of 0.78.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

A slowed-down copy of 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF (observed, not proved). Read this machine's states A as A, B as B, D as C, E as E, F as F of the other machine. Then 4,995,966 of this machine's first 107 configurations (tape, head position and state) are configurations of the other machine, in the same order. The last one is step 9,999,982 here and step 6,664,008 there, so this machine takes about 1.5 times as many steps. At most 229 steps pass here between two such configurations. The tables are not renamings of each other. Lean proves (lean/Twin.lean here, sim_or_break, not_halts_of_noBreak) that each step of the faster machine is matched by one or three steps of the slower one up to the first break, a configuration where the paired states act differently, and that neither machine halts if no break ever comes. A halt of either machine is itself a break, and the halting transitions of the two do not correspond, so the two are not known to halt together.

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB---_0RC1RD_1LA0LA_1LE0RB_1LF1LE_1LC0LD: rename A→F, B→C, C→A, D→B, E→D, F→E and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RB_1LC---_0LA1LD_1RE0LC_1RF1RE_1RA0RD: rename A→F, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→E; it is this table started in state B
  • 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_1RE0RE_1LF---_0LD1LA: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→F, E→A, F→B; it is this table started in state E
  • 1RB1RA_1RC0RF_1RD0RD_1LE---_0LC1LF_1RA0LE: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→F, F→A; it is this table started in state F

summary: A slower twin of 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF: the same running-parity (Sierpinski) word in 4-cell letters 1110/1111, with the same epochs; at the epoch starts the two machines have identical tapes, head position and state.
